key_terms.meaning: A blueprint written with the class keyword that groups data attributes and behaviour methods under one name.
One instance created from a class, holding its own copy of the instance attributes.
A named value stored in an object (instance attribute) or shared by a class (class attribute).
A function defined inside a class; its first parameter, self, refers to the calling object.
The initialiser Python calls automatically right after an object is created, used to set instance attributes.
The first parameter of an instance method; it holds the object on which the method was called.
The finaliser Python calls when an object is about to be destroyed, that is, when its reference count falls to zero.
Bundling data with the methods that work on it, and hiding the data behind a controlled interface.
An accessor (getter) returns an attribute value; a mutator (setter) changes it, usually after a validity check.
Python rewrites an attribute written as __x inside a class to _ClassName__x, which discourages outside access.
A subclass receives the attributes and methods of a parent class and may add to or change that behaviour.
Built-in that returns a proxy calling the next class in the method resolution order, usually the parent's version.
The ordered list of classes Python searches, using C3 linearization, when it looks up a method on an object.
Defining in a subclass a method with the same name as a parent method, so subclass objects use the new version.
The same call such as obj.area() runs different code depending on the object's actual class, chosen at runtime.
Giving an operator new meaning for a class by defining dunder methods such as __add__ for + and __eq__ for ==.
Python uses an object if it has the needed method, without checking its class: if it quacks like a duck, treat it as one.
A class from the abc module that cannot be instantiated until every @abstractmethod in it is implemented by a subclass.
An object whose __iter__ returns itself and whose __next__ returns the next item or raises StopIteration.
A function containing yield; calling it returns a generator object that produces values lazily, one per next().
A callable that takes a function or class and returns a wrapped version with added behaviour, applied with @name.

takeaways: A class is a blueprint and an object is one built instance; each object keeps its own instance attributes while methods are shared.
__init__ runs automatically after creation to set up state, self is the hidden first argument that binds a call to one object, and __del__ runs when the object is destroyed.
Encapsulation protects state behind accessor and mutator methods; name mangling with __ discourages direct access but does not forbid it.
Inheritance lets a subclass reuse a parent, and super() reaches the next class in the MRO so parent code still runs.
Overriding replaces a parent method, and Python finds the method by walking the class's MRO, which C3 linearization builds left to right.
Polymorphism and duck typing mean Python decides which method body to run from the object itself at runtime, not from a declared type.
An abstract base class fixes the interface and blocks instantiation until subclasses implement every abstract method.
Iterators, generators and decorators let you produce values lazily and wrap behaviour without editing the original function.
bank_note: Long answers here almost always ask for a definition plus a complete runnable Python program, so define the term, show the class code, and show the output.

bank.q: Define a class and an object. With a Python class for a student record, explain how attributes and methods are written, and show that two objects keep independent state.
outline: class keyword, class name, indented body
instance attributes created in __init__ with self.name = value
method defined inside the class body taking self
two objects created; changing one object's attribute does not change the other
short runnable program and its printed output

bank.q: Explain the purpose of __init__ and self in Python classes. Write a class BankAccount that sets an opening balance in __init__, and state what error occurs if self is left out of a method definition.
outline: __init__ called automatically by the interpreter after object creation
self is the reference to the current object, bound automatically on obj.method()
code: class BankAccount with __init__(self, balance)
leaving out self gives TypeError: method takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
one class, many objects, each with its own balance

bank.q: Explain encapsulation and abstraction in Python. Show how a double underscore attribute is name-mangled, and write accessor and mutator methods that validate input.
outline: encapsulation: data plus methods, hidden internal state
abstraction: only the safe public methods are shown to the user
__balance becomes _ClassName__balance in the object's __dict__
get_balance() accessor and set_balance() mutator with a check for negative values
note that Python relies on convention, not on a compiler check

bank.q: Explain single, multiple and hierarchical inheritance with one small Python example of each, and state the purpose of super().
outline: single: class Car(Vehicle)
multiple: class Child(Father, Mother)
hierarchical: two subclasses of one parent
syntax class Sub(Parent): and calling Parent.__init__ through super().__init__()
diamond shape in multiple inheritance and why the MRO matters

bank.q: Write a Python class Rational with numerator and denominator, supporting +, == and printing through __str__. Reduce the fraction using math.gcd and raise an error for a zero denominator.
outline: __init__(self, num, den) with gcd reduction and denominator check
__add__ returning a new Rational, not mutating self
__eq__ comparing cross products or reduced values
__str__ returning '3/4' style text
sample run showing a + b, a == b and print(a)

bank.q: Write a class Shape with a method area, and subclasses Circle and Rectangle that call super().__init__() and override area. Print the MRO of Circle using Circle.mro().
outline: parent __init__ stores a name, subclasses pass it up with super().__init__(name)
override area in each subclass
loop over a list of shapes and call area() on each
Circle.mro() output including object at the end
explanation of why super() is better than naming the parent class

bank.q: Write a decorator that prints the time taken by a function, and a generator function that yields the first n Fibonacci numbers. Show the output for n = 6 and explain why the generator uses less memory.
outline: decorator taking func, inner wrapper using *args and **kwargs, returning wrapper
@timer applied above the function definition
generator using yield inside a loop, no list built
next() calls or a for loop producing 6 values
comparison: generator holds one value at a time, list holds all n

bank.q: Using the abc module, write an abstract base class Vehicle with abstract methods fuel_type and max_speed, then two concrete subclasses. Show what happens when Vehicle itself is instantiated.
outline: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
class Vehicle(ABC) with @abstractmethod decorated methods
subclasses implement both methods
instantiating Vehicle raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class
abstract class may still contain normal concrete methods

bank.q: Write a custom iterator class Countdown that counts from n down to 1, using __iter__ and __next__. Then rewrite the same logic as a generator function and compare the two.
outline: __iter__ returns self
__next__ returns the value and raises StopIteration at the end
__next__ must advance internal state
generator version using while n > 0: yield n
iterator needs a class and stored state; generator is shorter and pauses automatically

bank.q: Analyse how Python resolves a method call on an object. Explain the MRO, C3 linearization, and the order in which the classes of a diamond hierarchy are searched, with a code trace.
outline: attribute lookup: instance __dict__, then class, then parents in MRO
MRO always starts with the class itself and ends with object
C3 merges parent MROs preserving local precedence order
diamond: class D(B, C) gives D, B, C, A, object
verify with D.__mro__ or D.mro() and show which method body wins

bank.q: Compare inheritance-based polymorphism with duck typing in Python. Give a case where duck typing is better and a case where an abstract base class is safer.
outline: polymorphism through a common parent and overridden methods
duck typing: only the method name matters, no shared parent needed
duck typing suits small scripts and third-party objects, keeps coupling low
abstract base class documents the contract and catches missing methods early
isinstance checks vs try/except AttributeError trade-off

bank.q: Evaluate the claim that Python supports true encapsulation. Use name mangling, the single underscore convention and the property decorator in your answer.
outline: no private keyword; access control is by convention
_x is a hint, __x is mangled to _Class__x but still reachable
mangling breaks in inheritance and in dir() output it is visible
property decorator gives controlled get and set without changing call syntax
verdict: encapsulation is supported by design discipline, not enforced by the language

bank.q: Design a small library system for a college using classes, inheritance, an abstract base class and operator overloading, and justify each design choice for a long answer.
outline: class Book with title, author, copies and __str__ and __eq__
abstract base class Member with borrow and return_item as abstract methods
Student and Faculty as subclasses using super().__init__()
encapsulation of the copies count with accessor and mutator
justification: reuse, safe interface, polymorphism in a loop over members

bank.q: Define the terms class, object, method, instance attribute, constructor and destructor as used in Python, and give the name of the special method used for each of the last two.
outline: class: blueprint; object: instance
method: function in a class body with self as first parameter
instance attribute: stored per object, usually created in __init__
constructor/initialiser: __init__
destructor/finaliser: __del__

glossary.def: A user-defined blueprint that groups attributes and methods.
A single value created from a class, also called an instance.
A value stored in one object, normally created as self.name in __init__.
A value defined directly in the class body and shared by all objects of that class.
A function defined inside a class that works on an object.
The parameter that refers to the object a method was called on.
The initialiser method Python runs automatically to set up a new object.
The finaliser method that runs when an object is about to be destroyed.
The method that returns the friendly text printed by print(obj) and used by str(obj).
A special method with two leading and two trailing underscores that Python calls for built-in operations.
Keeping data and its methods together and hiding the data behind a controlled interface.
Showing only the essential operations of an object and hiding the details of how they work.
A getter method that returns the value of a private attribute.
A setter method that changes an attribute after checking the new value.
The automatic renaming of an attribute __x to _ClassName__x.
The mechanism by which a subclass reuses the attributes and methods of a parent class.
A class defined with another class in parentheses, gaining its members.
A built-in returning a proxy that calls the next method in the MRO.
The list of classes Python searches, in C3 order, to find an attribute or method.
Replacing a parent method with a subclass method of the same name.
One call producing different behaviour according to the object's class at runtime.
Using an object based on the methods it has rather than on its class.
The ambiguity in multiple inheritance when two parents share a common grandparent.
A class that declares methods which subclasses must implement and that cannot be instantiated.
Any object that can give an iterator, for example a list, string or file.
An object produced by a function containing yield, giving values lazily.
A callable that wraps a function or class to add behaviour, written above it with @name.
